name: sim_carnot_axis4_cycle_ordering_bridge
claim: The Carnot cycle direction (clockwise in P-V = heat engine) IS Axis 4 (loop ordering / composition direction). Forward composition extracts work (W > 0); reversed composition requires work input (W < 0). Non-commutativity of thermodynamic steps captures the Axis 4 asymmetry. The Axis 4 sign IS the bivector orientation of the cycle in (entropy, temperature) space.

pytorch.reason: represent each Carnot step as volume/pressure transformation; compute work W = integral P dV numerically via torch; verify W_forward > 0, W_reverse < 0, sum = 0; load-bearing

pyg.reason: no graph learning required; probe operates on density matrices not graph structures

z3.reason: UNSAT: W_forward > 0 AND W_reverse > 0 simultaneously — Second Law as structural UNSAT; can't extract positive work from both directions; load-bearing

cvc5.reason: z3 sufficient for all separability and product-form UNSAT proofs in this sim

sympy.reason: symbolic Carnot W_total = Q_H*(1 - T_C/T_H); derive dW/d(Axis4 orientation param); load-bearing

clifford.reason: Carnot cycle as closed path in Cl(2,0): e1=entropy, e2=temperature; forward = e1^e2 (positive bivector), reverse = e2^e1 = -e1^e2 (negative bivector); Axis 4 sign IS the bivector orientation; load-bearing

geomstats.reason: no Riemannian manifold computation required; geometry handled analytically

e3nn.reason: no SO(3)-equivariant neural network computation required in this probe

rustworkx.reason: forward Carnot step graph (4-cycle clockwise) vs reverse (counterclockwise); distinct directed graphs with opposite winding; load-bearing

xgi.reason: hyperedge {step1, step2, step3, step4, Axis4}: all four steps plus orientation axis form a 5-way relationship; load-bearing

toponetx.reason: no chain complex or cell complex computation required in this probe

gudhi.reason: no persistent homology or Rips complex computation required in this probe

P1_forward_carnot_positive_work.note: Forward Carnot (clockwise): W > 0; maps to Axis 4 = forward composition order

P2_reverse_carnot_negative_work.note: Reverse Carnot (counterclockwise): W < 0 (work input); maps to Axis 4 = reversed order

P3_forward_plus_reverse_zero.note: W_forward + W_reverse = 0: reversible cycle (forward and reverse cancel exactly)

P4_cycle_returns_to_start.note: Forward Carnot cycle returns to start: delta_S = 0, delta_T = 0

P5_noncommutativity_thermodynamic_steps.note: step1 then step3 gives W > 0; step3 then step1 reverses sign: steps do not commute

P6_sympy_work_TC_derivative.note: dW/dT_C = -Q_H/T_H < 0; reversing Axis 4 (T_C <-> T_H) changes sign of work gradient

P7_pytorch_numerical_integration.note: pytorch numerical integration of P dV: W_total > 0 for forward Carnot cycle

P8_clifford_axis4_bivector_orientation.note: Forward Carnot = positive bivector (+e12); Reverse = negative (-e12): Axis 4 IS bivector sign

P9_rustworkx_forward_reverse_distinct_gr.note: Forward and reverse Carnot are distinct directed 4-cycles: Axis 4 = which direction the cycle runs

P10_xgi_cycle_axis4_hyperedge.note: All 4 Carnot steps + Axis 4 orientation form a 5-way hyperedge: Axis 4 is an irreducible part

N1_z3_second_law_work_unsat.note: UNSAT: W_fwd > 0 AND W_rev = -W_fwd AND W_rev > 0 simultaneously => Second Law as UNSAT

N2_irreversible_cycle_asymmetric.note: Irreversible cycle: W_fwd + W_rev != 0; Axis 4 symmetry broken by irreversibility

N3_efficiency_asymmetric_at_equal_temps.note: At T_C=T_H: forward eta=0 (no work); reverse COP->inf (pure heat pumping): Axis 4 asymmetry

N4_sympy_efficiency_asymmetric_swap.note: Swapping T_H and T_C changes eta: efficiency is Axis 4 asymmetric

N5_clifford_forward_reverse_cancel.note: Forward + reverse bivectors cancel: Axis 4 forward and reverse are exact opposites

B1_Tc_to_zero_max_work.note: T_C -> 0: eta -> 1, W -> Q_H; Axis 4 forward asymmetry is maximal

B2_TC_eq_TH_zero_work.note: T_C = T_H: W = 0; Axis 4 ordering has no thermodynamic consequence

B3_pytorch_work_monotone_in_TC.note: W decreases as T_C increases: Axis 4 asymmetry scales with temperature gradient

B4_rustworkx_4cycle_degree_one.note: Carnot cycle is a directed 4-cycle: each step has in-degree=out-degree=1

B5_xgi_Axis4_node_degree_one.note: Axis4 node has degree=1: appears only in the full cycle ordering hyperedge
